events.body:
C1: RydeX is a non-metered service and the only disputed charge is the $6.61 cancellation fee; because the driver cancelled while alleging a rider no-show, the charge stands only if NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are all met (F4, F7). [F4 F7] [NS-0 NS-1]
C2: Requirement (iii) fails: after the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 he remained within 200 m of the pickup for only 1 min 40 s, far short of the required continuous wait of more than 3 minutes (F6, F5). [F6 F5] [NS-1 NS-2]
C3: The system records confirm the wait was under three minutes in total: the driver's cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 2 min 25 s, and the platform-recorded arrival to cancellation gap was likewise 2 min 25 s (F2, F5). [F2 F5] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: The driver's own message shows he cancelled before any three-minute wait had run, writing "3 min up, cancelling the trip" at 14:15, only about a minute and a half after his arrival tap (F10, F6). [F10 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]

claims.assertion: RydeX is a non-metered service and the only disputed charge is the $6.61 cancellation fee; because the driver cancelled while alleging a rider no-show, the charge stands only if NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are all met (F4, F7).

Requirement (iii) fails: after the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 he remained within 200 m of the pickup for only 1 min 40 s, far short of the required continuous wait of more than 3 minutes (F6, F5).

The system records confirm the wait was under three minutes in total: the driver's cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 2 min 25 s, and the platform-recorded arrival to cancellation gap was likewise 2 min 25 s (F2, F5).
The driver's own message shows he cancelled before any three-minute wait had run, writing "3 min up, cancelling the trip" at 14:15, only about a minute and a half after his arrival tap (F10, F6).

Nothing beyond the driver's bare assertion supports a no-show; his post-trip claim that he "waited for the rider, then cancelled as a no-show" is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records showing a stationary period of only 2 min 0 s at 41 m and a sub-three-minute wait (F12, F3, F2, F5).
Because NS-1 is not satisfied and the driver, not the rider, cancelled, no cancellation fee is chargeable and the $6.61 must be refunded in full to the rider (F4, F7).
The driver already has one upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days, so this repeat of the same conduct warrants attaching the account-review action to the rider's refund (F17).
The rider's own record is clean — 3.3-year account, 4.7 rating, zero upheld disputes in 90 days — so nothing on her side undercuts the complaint (F16).

weaknesses: The driver did satisfy NS-1 (i) and (ii): he tapped "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 and was only 41 m from the pickup at that moment (F6, F3), so the other side will say the sole contested element is the short wait, and point to the platform arrival at 14:13:25 (F5).

The driver's chat message "3 min up" (F10) can be read as his claim that three minutes had elapsed; the rider's reply is the system records F2, F5 and F6 showing at most 2 min 25 s inside 200 m, which win under the record-priority rule, but a judge might treat F10 as merely ambiguous.

The rider sent no messages of her own (F9–F11 contain only the driver's texts), so the case rests almost entirely on the driver's failure to meet the wait threshold rather than on any evidence of the rider's promptness at the pickup.

Requirement (iii) fails: after the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 he remained within 200 m of the pickup for only 1 min 40 s, far short of the required continuous wait of more than 3 minutes (F6, F5).

The system records confirm the wait was under three minutes in total: the driver's cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 2 min 25 s, and the platform-recorded arrival to cancellation gap was likewise 2 min 25 s (F2, F5).
The driver's own message shows he cancelled before any three-minute wait had run, writing "3 min up, cancelling the trip" at 14:15, only about a minute and a half after his arrival tap (F10, F6).

Nothing beyond the driver's bare assertion supports a no-show; his post-trip claim that he "waited for the rider, then cancelled as a no-show" is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records showing a stationary period of only 2 min 0 s at 41 m and a sub-three-minute wait (F12, F3, F2, F5).
Because NS-1 is not satisfied and the driver, not the rider, cancelled, no cancellation fee is chargeable and the $6.61 must be refunded in full to the rider (F4, F7).

weaknesses: The driver did satisfy NS-1 (i) and (ii): he tapped "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 and was only 41 m from the pickup at that moment (F6, F3), so the other side will say the sole contested element is the short wait, and point to the platform arrival at 14:13:25 (F5).

The driver's chat message "3 min up" (F10) can be read as his claim that three minutes had elapsed; the rider's reply is the system records F2, F5 and F6 showing at most 2 min 25 s inside 200 m, which win under the record-priority rule, but a judge might treat F10 as merely ambiguous.

The rider sent no messages of her own (F9–F11 contain only the driver's texts), so the case rests almost entirely on the driver's failure to meet the wait threshold rather than on any evidence of the rider's promptness at the pickup.

claims.assertion: The driver completed every arrival formality: the platform recorded arrival at the pickup point at 14:13:25 (F5) and the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 (F6), so NS-1(i) is met and the arrival was a driver tap, not an automatic determination.

At the moment of the tap the GPS placed the driver 41 m from the pickup point (F6), well inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1(ii) is met; the closest approach over the whole episode was 38 m (F1).

The driver remained within 200 m of the pickup continuously for 1 min 40 s after the tap, until the cancellation at 14:15:50 (F6), and was stationary 41 m from the pickup from 14:13:50 to 14:15:50 (F3); measured from the tap, the driver waited 100 seconds, not the 3 minutes NS-1(iii) requires.

The driver's own in-app message at 14:15 announces "3 min up, cancelling the trip" (F10), but the system records show the tap at 14:14:10 and cancellation at 14:15:50, i.e. 1 min 40 s later (F6); the chat cannot be built on as establishing the three-minute wait.

The driver's written statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited for the rider, then cancelled as a no-show" (F12) is a post-trip assertion about his own state of mind and cannot cure the short wait measured by the GPS and timeline records (F6, F3).

The rider's own account is partly corroborated: she says the driver cancelled "after barely two minutes" (complaint), which matches the 2 min 25 s from platform-recorded arrival to cancellation (F5) and the 2 min 0 s stationary period (F3); she was not kept waiting long.

The cancellation fee on record is $6.61 (F7, F4) with no surge applied (F8), so if the wait is measured from the "I'm Here" tap as NS-1 requires, the fee does not stand and the refundable amount is the full $6.61.

weaknesses: The whole fee turns on one measurement: F6 shows the driver stayed within 200 m for only 1 min 40 s after the 14:14:10 tap, which is below the 3-minute bar in NS-1(iii); counting from first entering the radius at 14:13:25 (F2, F5) gives only 2 min 25 s, still short.

The driver's own 14:15 message "3 min up, cancelling the trip" (F10) contradicts the system timeline (F6) and will be used to show he believed he had met a threshold he had not met; the system clock wins on the facts.
